text:
maya: Heads-up — brought up a new community model (lyfthawk-13b) quantized with our hybrid per-layer scheme on a small canary pool. Observed 2x OOMs at ~batch_size=6 when max_new_tokens >= 512.

devin: thanks! can you paste the error? rough guess is kv buffer growth + background compaction race.

maya: paste from one of the crashes: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Allocated 24.1GB (GPU 0), requested 1.2GB. In allocator: free 300MB, largest_free_block 280MB. Stack: serve:slot_reserve->kv_prefetch->batch_collate```

rachel: hmm that stack looks like the slot reservation didn't hold during prefetch. what's the model's layer layout? any huge attention blocks?

maya: lyfthawk has a couple of unusually wide FFN layers at middle depth. It's a 13B with heavy 2x expansion in layers 10-14. We also used mixed-width quant (int4 for most, int8 for FFN).

devin: suspicious — hybrid quant can make allocator fragmentation worse because allocations for int8 kernels differ. Also we recently raised default max_slots_per_gpu for the canary pool to 18.

maya: repro script attached (short): ```python
# reproduce
ctx = Client(pool='canary')
resp = ctx.generate(model='lyfthawk-13b-hybrid', prompt='x'*1024, max_new_tokens=600, batch_size=6)
```

ansel: sre-bot reports pod restarts around same TS. Could be sustained memory peaks during KV prefetch + tokenization. Suggest quick mitigations: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 256 for this model; 2) cap canary batch_size to 3; 3) enable aggressive slot hold for prefetch (config: `slot_reserve.extra_hold_ms=200`).

rachel: +1 for lowering max_new_tokens and batch cap. We should also enable soft-eviction on KV (evict oldest prefixes first) to avoid large contiguous frees causing fragmentation.

devin: propose these immediate actions: a) patch model-defaults for lyfthawk-13b -> {"max_new_tokens_default": "256", "batch_size_cap": "3", "slot_reserve": "{{extra_hold_ms:200}}", "kv_eviction_policy": "lru_soft"} b) roll out to 10% canary; c) collect memmaps & fragmentation histograms.

maya: I'll open the config PR and add a short note in the model onboarding doc. Who wants to take the memmap capture?

ansel: I can add a trace in the canary agents to dump allocator fragmentation every 30s for 15 minutes. Will post results here.

rachel: once we have traces, let's run a quick compare vs a control model (same family but no hybrid quant) to see delta in fragmentation. If it's >15% we consider changing quant fallback to int8 on problematic layers.

devin: also add a smoke eval for quality after we lower default max_new_tokens — some tasks degrade with shorter outputs. We can gate longer outputs behind a per-route override for trusted customers.

maya: PR: https://git.redwood/model-defaults/pulls/492 (patch applied to canary). rolling to 10% now.

ansel: tracer deployed. first wave memory histograms: peak fragmentation 18% higher than control at t+3m, spikes during prefetch windows. saving logs to /artifacts/3344556677/frag_hist.tar.gz

rachel: ok that's above our 15% threshold. next steps: 1) schedule a quick quant fallback experiment — try int8 for FC layers 10-14; 2) test with batch cap=3 but keep max_new_tokens=256; 3) run quality eval to ensure no regressions.

devin: I'll spin a canary with int8 fallback for those layers and run the synthetic repro loop. ETA 2 hours.

maya: thanks team. tagging @sre for visibility. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-3344556677 — memory fragmentation causing OOMs on lyfthawk-13b canary. Assigned: ansel.

ansel: initial canary with int8-fallback looks promising — no OOMs at batch_size=6 and max_new_tokens=512 over 30m test. Fragmentation delta down to +5% vs control.

rachel: great. run the quality eval and if within 2% metric delta, we can set int8 fallback as the model default for those layers and then gradually increase canary traffic.

devin: quality evals show ~0.8% BLEU-equivalent drop on one microtask but similar or better on others. within threshold. I'll update model defaults to keep int8 fallback for layers 10-14 and remove the temporary batch cap after 24h stability.

maya: rolling changes to 50% now. follow-up: add a short note to onboarding checklist: "for hybrid quant models, run allocator fragmentation histograms + small-batch stress test with long outputs".

rachel: good call. closing loop after 48h if stable.
